ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.claim: Islahi wonders at people who boast of Abrahamic or Mosaic association and expect high rank while withholding charity, since those scriptures teach that no one bears another's burden and each faces the fruit of his own deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r5.anchor: the most prominent teaching of Abraham (sws) and Moses (sws) was that in the Hereafter no one will bear the burden of another person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r3.claim: The Quraysh and People of the Book dream of Paradise through alleged intercession, but the teachings of Moses and Abraham say no soul bears another’s burden.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r3.anchor: in the Hereafter no soul shall bear the burden of another?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r2.claim: The rule that no soul bears another’s burden is taught in Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures and refutes baseless intercession, the sūrah’s subject.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r2.anchor: This in fact is a refutation of the baseless concept of intercession which is the subject of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r3.claim: The Torah and Injil repeatedly teach this rule, making it surprising that their recipients were led by Satan into polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r3.anchor: This teaching is mentioned in the Torah and the Injil at so many instances

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r4.claim: The lightened in is a substitute for mā in “what is in the scriptures,” or stands nominative as a clarification of their contents: no bearer bears another's burden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p24/r4.anchor: وإن هي المخففة من الثقيلة، وهي بدل من ما في قوله: بما في صحف، أو في موضع رفع

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r1.claim: أن is a lightened form of الثقيلة with an omitted pronoun of شأن as subject; لا تزر is predicate. Negation is used because the predicate is a finite verbal clause without قد.
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r1.anchor: " أن " مخففة من الثقيلة، واسمها محذوف هو ضمير الشأن. ولا تزر هو الخبر وجيء بالنفي

SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r2.claim: The preferred case makes أن and its clause genitive as بدل from ما in بما في صحف.
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r2.anchor: أظهرهما: الجر بدلا من " ما " في قوله: { بما في صحف }.

SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is nominative as predicate of an omitted هو or ذلك, answering “What is in their scrolls?”
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r3.anchor: الرفع خبرا لمبتدأ مضمر أي: ذلك أن لا تزر أو هو أن لا تزر، وهو جواب لسؤال مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r4.claim: Al-Samīn also allows an accusative with omitted أعني; wherever the omitted subject is used this way, that verb is also omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:53:38/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نصبا بإضمار أعني جوابا لذلك السائل. وكل موضع أضمر فيه هذا المبتدأ لهذا المعنى أضمر فيه هذا الفعل.

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r1.claim: The Qur'an repeats this ethical law in five places; this occurrence is earliest in revelation chronology.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r1.anchor: This basic ethical law appears in the Qur'an five times - in 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, as well as in the above instance, which is the oldest

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r2.claim: The principle rejects the Christian doctrine of original sin and inherited human guilt.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r2.anchor: it expresses a categorical rejection of the Christian doctrine of the

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r3.claim: It also rejects atonement for a person's sins through a saint's or prophet's sacrifice, including Christian vicarious atonement and Persian redemption by Mithras.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r3.anchor: it refutes the idea that a person's sins could be

ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r4.claim: By implication, the law rules out mediation between the sinner and God.
ASAD-NOTES:53:38#n31/r4.anchor: it denies, by implication, the possibility of any

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Aws says people were once held for another person's sin until Abraham came and God established that no bearer bears another's burden.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإبراهيم الذي وفى ﴾ قال كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره حتى جاء إبراهيم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Kursī is the place of the two feet, while no one can measure the Throne.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#2/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال الكرسي موضع القدمين والعرش لا يقدر أحد قدره

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Aws says that before Abraham's revelation, a person could be seized for another's sin; the principle then declared that no bearer bears another's burden.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#2/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس قال كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره عتى نزل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r1.claim: أن is a lightened form of heavy أنَّ with an omitted subject pronoun referring to the matter; the negative clause is its predicate and replaces material in Moses’ scrolls or predicates an omitted subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r1.anchor: على أن ( أن ) هي المخففة من الثقيلة وضمير الشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r2.claim: No person is punished for another’s sin so that the other can escape punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r2.anchor: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره ليتخلص الثاني عن عقابه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r3.claim: The Prophet’s warning that an originator of an evil practice bears its burden and followers’ burdens is no contradiction: misleading others is the originator’s own sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p66/r3.anchor: من سن سنة سيئة فعليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r1.claim: No person is taken to account for another person’s sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r1.anchor: أي: لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل أخرى، ومعناه: لا تؤخذ نفس بإثم غيرها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r2.claim: This principle refutes the claim made to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra that someone would bear his sin for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r2.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال قول من ضمن للوليد بن المغيرة بأنه يحمل عنه الإثم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r3.speaker: عكرمة، ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that before Abraham people punished one person for another’s killing, including killing a parent, child, sibling, wife, or slave; Abraham forbade this and conveyed God’s rule.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p415/r3.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: كانوا قبل إبراهيم عليه السلام يأخذون الرجل بذنب غيره، كان الرجل يقتل بقتل أبيه وابنه وأخيه

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled the principle that no burdened soul bears another's burden, through the passage continuing to the ancient scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت {والنجم} فبلغ {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: وفى {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى} إلى قوله {من النذر الأولى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says Abraham carried out and conveyed the rule that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: أدى عن ربه {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.speaker: عمرو بن أوس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.claim: Amr ibn Aws says people were once punished for another's sin until Abraham conveyed that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن أوس قال: كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره حتى جاء إبراهيم فقال الله {وإبراهيم الذي وفى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says that before Abraham people held a close relative responsible for another, until Abraham conveyed that no one is taken for another's sin.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: كانوا قبل إبراهيم يأخذون الولي بالمولى حتى كان إبراهيم فبلغ {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.speaker: هذيل بن شرحبيل
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.claim: Hudhayl ibn Shurayhil says another's sin was borne from Noah to Abraham, who brought the rule that no soul bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p660/r6.anchor: عن هذيل بن شرحبيل قال: كان الرجل يؤخذ بذنب غيره فيما بين نوح إلى إبراهيم حتى جاء إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r1.claim: The clause may be an appositional specification of the general contents of Moses' and Abraham's scriptures, with أن reduced from أنَّ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون بدلا من ما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم بدل مفصل من مجمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, أن is explanatory because the written material in the scriptures conveys speech in meaning, allowing an explanatory clause to interpret it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ( أن ) تفسيرية فسرت ما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم لأن ما من الصحف شيء مكتوب والكتابة فيها معنى القول دون حروفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r3.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites a report that everything from 53:36 through 53:56 was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر القرطبي عند تفسير قوله تعالى : { هذا نذير من النذر الأولى } ( النجم : 56 ) في هذه السورة عن السدي عن أبي صالح قال : هذه الحروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r4.claim: Taziru is the imperfect of wazara, meaning to commit or bear a burden of sin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r4.anchor: و { تزر } مضارع وزر ، إذا فعل وزرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r5.claim: The feminine forms are understood as nafs; their use under negation makes the statement universal and rejects al-Walid ibn al-Mughira's claim that another could bear his punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r5.anchor: وتأنيث { وازرة } بتأويل : نفس ، وكذلك تأنيث { أخرى } ، ووقوع ( نفس ) و { أخرى } في سياق النفي يفيد العموم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r6.claim: The principle appears in Abraham's scriptures and parallels Abraham's prayer in 26:87–89 that he not be shamed on resurrection day, when wealth and children will not help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r6.anchor: وهذا مما كان في صحف إبراهيم ، ومنه ما حكى الله في قوله : { ولا تخزني يوم يبعثون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r7.claim: The Torah account of Abraham's plea for Lot's people likewise asks whether the righteous would be destroyed with the wicked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r7.anchor: وحكي في التوراة عن إبراهيم أنه قال في شأن قوم لوط : ( أفتهلك البار مع الآثم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r8.claim: The Torah says parents are not killed for their children or children for their parents, and Moses asks whether God would destroy Israel for the fools among them; 7:155 is linked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r8.anchor: وأما نظيره في صحف موسى ففي التوراة ( لا يقتل الآباء عن الأولاد ولا يقتل الأولاد عن الآباء كل إنسان بخطيئته يقتل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r9.claim: The unqualified word burden makes the principle apply to worldly as well as afterlife matters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r9.anchor: وعموم لفظ { وزر } يقتضي اطراد الحكم في أمور الدنيا وأمور الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r10.claim: The Torah warning that God visits parents' sins on descendants for three generations concerns worldly chains of cause and effect, not transfer of guilt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r10.anchor: فذلك في ترتيب المسببات على الأسباب الدنيوية وهو تحذير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r11.claim: A person who leads others into sin incurs additional punishment for misleading them, not someone else's transferred guilt; 16:25 supports this distinction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r11.anchor: ولكنه من قبيل زيادة العقاب لأجل تضليل الغير ، قال تعالى : { ليحملوا أوزارهم كاملة يوم القيامة ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم بغير علم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r12.claim: A hadith says the first son of Adam bears a share of every unjust killing because he initiated murder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130#2/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( ما من نفس تقتل ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأولل كفل من دمها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80/r1.claim: The scrolls state that no burden-bearing soul carries another’s burden; no one is punished for another person’s sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p80/r1.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل أخرى والمعنى لا تؤخذ بإثم غيرها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r1.claim: No soul bears another soul's sin; w-z-r means to incur a burden of sin, that is, wrongdoing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r1.anchor: تز من وزر يزر اذا اكتسب وزرا وهو الاثم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r2.claim: “An” is lightened from the emphatic particle, with an implicit pronoun of the matter; the clause is genitive as a substitute for “in the scrolls of Moses,” or nominative as the predicate of “it is.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192/r2.anchor: والضمير ضمير الشان ومحل ان وما بعدهاالجر

STUDYQURAN:53:38/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r1.claim: This Quranic axiom first occurs here in chronological revelation order.
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r1.anchor: This is the first instance of this Quranic axiom in the chronological order of revelation

STUDYQURAN:53:38/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r2.claim: No one is forced to endure punishment accrued through another person’s deeds.
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r2.anchor: No one will be forced to endure the punishments accrued through deeds committed by another

STUDYQURAN:53:38/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r3.claim: A famous hadith says whoever establishes a sinful custom bears its burden and that of everyone following it until Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r3.anchor: as in a famous ḥadīth: “Whosoever establishes a sinful custom

STUDYQURAN:53:38/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r4.claim: Those who lead others astray receive double punishment.
STUDYQURAN:53:38/r4.anchor: those who lead others astray are said to have “a double punishment”

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.claim: People's striving differs: worldly pursuit loses, pursuit of Paradise profits, disciplining the self reaches God's approval, and striving in spiritual aspiration is thanked by God and guided to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r10.anchor: الناس في سعيهم مختلفون ؛ فمن كان سعيه في طلب الدنيا خسرت صفقته ، ومن كان سعيه في طلب الجنة ربحت صفقته

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.claim: A sinner who strives to seek forgiveness and regrets the darkening of his record will receive reward, nearness, honor, and intimacy from God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r11.anchor: وأما المذنب - فإذا كان سعيه في طلب غفرانه ، وندم القلب على ما اسود من ديوانه ، فسوف يجد من الله الثواب والقربة والكرامة والزلفة

TAB-FULL:v22p79/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r1.claim: Each sinner bears their own sin; this passage rebuts a promise to carry al-Walid ibn al-Mughira's punishment for him.
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r1.anchor: وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v22p79/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r2.speaker: أبو مالك الغفاري
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r2.claim: Abu Malik al-Ghifari says the passage from verses 38 through 56 is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
TAB-FULL:v22p79/r2.anchor: عن أبي مالك الغفاري، في قوله: {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى} [النجم: 39] إلى قوله: {من النذر الأولى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r4.claim: On the second view, an may be genitive as an appositive to what was in the scriptures, meaning that no soul bears another's sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r4.anchor: خفض على البدل من قوله: {بما في صحف}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r5.claim: Alternatively, an may be nominative with an omitted pronoun, as if asking what the scriptures contain and answering that no burden-bearer bears another's burden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r5.anchor: وقال: يجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على إضمار هو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r6.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r6.claim: The verse means that no man is held responsible for another person's sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r6.anchor: قال عكرمة عن ابن عباس: لا يؤخذ الرجل بذنب غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r7.claim: The verse refutes the offer to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira that someone could give him payment and carry his sins; no one is punished for another's crime.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r7.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال لقول من قال للوليد بن المغيرة: أعطني شيئا وأحمل عنك ذنوبك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r8.claim: The author reports that exegetes say from Noah until Abraham, a person was taken for the sins of a brother or son, until Abraham conveyed this teaching; it applies in both worldly life and the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r8.anchor: فقالوا: كان من لدن نوح إلى زمان إبراهيم يؤخذ الرجل بذنب أخيه وابنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r9.claim: The Prophet also taught that one who calls people to error bears a burden like the burdens of those who follow, as stated in 16:25.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p66/r9.anchor: وذكره رسولنا محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن من دعا إلى ضلالة كان عليه

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.claim: The scrolls passage and the statement that one burdened soul bears no other's burden correspond to 53:30–31, since both passages explain recompense.

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.claim: One possible object of يرى is the belief that one person's burden is carried by another: the man supposes this while unaware that each bears only his own.

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.claim: The most apparent content is the rule that no bearer carries another's burden, though the phrase may cover more because the scrolls contain more than this alone.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.anchor: هو ما ذكر بقوله : { ألا تزر

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.claim: Rāzī explains Abraham's fulfillment by saying he kept his promise to seek forgiveness for his father and did so; God's refusal taught that each person receives only the fruits of his own effort and no soul bears another's sin.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r7.anchor: فاستغفر ووفى بالعهد ولم يغفر الله له

RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r1.claim: Rāzī takes ألا تزر as an appositive explaining بما: the scrolls' content is that no burdened soul bears another's burden; he recalls the alternatives that it may point to the better afterlife or foundational doctrines.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r1.anchor: هو ما بينه بقوله { ألا تزر

RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r2.claim: Here أن is the light form of heavy أن; lightening is obligatory before a following verb or a particle governing a verb, since a verb cannot itself govern another verb directly.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r2.anchor: أن خفيفة من الثقيلة كأنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r3.claim: وازرة means a soul expected to carry a burden, not one already loaded; thus the verse meaningfully denies that even a potential bearer takes on another's burden.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13#2/r3.anchor: المراد من الوازرة هي التي يتوقع منها الوزر والحمل لا التي وزرت وحملت

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham completed obedience through what he did with his son after the dream; the scrolls of Moses state that no bearer bears another's burden, through the rest of the verse.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى

TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.claim: The statement that no bearer bears another's burden is cited as material in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, not as a restriction defining what Abraham fulfilled.
TAB-FULL:v22p77/r9.anchor: فإن ذلك مما أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه في صحف موسى وإبراهيم، لا مما خص به الخبر

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r2.claim: An is the lightened emphatic particle with a hidden pronoun; the negative clause is its predicate and either an appositive to the scrolls' contents or a predicate of an omitted subject.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r2.anchor: الجملة المنفية خبرها ومحل الجملة الجر على أنها بدل مما في صحف موسى

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r3.claim: A wāzira is a soul expected to bear a burden, not one already weighed down; no person answers for another's sin or can take it over to save that person.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r3.anchor: فابمراد بالوازرة هي التي يتوقع منها الوزر والحمل لا التي وزرت وحملت ثقلا

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r4.claim: This rule disproves the promise made to al-Walīd that someone else would carry his punishment.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r4.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال قول من ضمن للوليد بن المغيرة أن يحمل عنه الإثم

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r5.claim: There is no conflict with the statement that killing one resembles killing all: the killer bears his own sin of causing and prompting later murders, not their direct acts.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r5.anchor: إذ ليس المعنى أن عليه إثم مباشرة سائر القاتلين بل المعنى أن عليه فوق إثم مباشرته للقتل المحظور

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says whoever institutes an evil practice bears its burden and followers' burdens; Bursevī explains these as the originator's own burden of misguidance.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله عليه السلام : من سن سيئة فعليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r3.claim: Wizr means a burden and is commonly used for sin; a bearing soul is one disposed to carry sin.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r3.anchor: الوزر الثقل وكثر استعماله في الإثم، والوازرة النفس

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r4.claim: The verse states what is in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures: no soul is charged with another soul’s sin or held accountable for it.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r4.anchor: لا تحمل نفس إثم نفس أخرى أي لا تتأثم نفس بما لنفس أخرى من الإثم فلا تؤاخذ نفس بإثم نفس أخرى

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.claim: This verse and the following scriptural statements introduced by ‘that’ belong to the set of seventeen verses drawn from the two scriptures.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r5.anchor: وكذا سائر الآيات المصدرة بأن وأن إلى تمام سبع عشرة آية

TABRISI:53:31-41/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-41/r10.claim: The phrase is understood as annahu lā taziru and substitutes for the preceding reference to what is in Moses' pages; mā is a relative pronoun.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r10.anchor: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى تقديره أنه لا تزر

TABRISI:53:32-39/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r15.claim: No soul carries another soul's burden, meaning no one is punished for another person's sin.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r15.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل أخرى والمعنى لا تؤخذ نفس بإثم غيرها

TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.claim: The clauses opened with anna are all treated as teachings in the pages of Abraham and Moses, following the report of what those pages contain.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r15.anchor: وإنما فتحت أن في هذه المواضع كلها لأن جميعها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

THALABI:v9p152#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152#2/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p152#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl reconciles the two burden passages: no soul voluntarily bears another's sin, while people bear others' burdens unwillingly.
THALABI:v9p152#2/r4.anchor: ما قال الحسين بن الفضل: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى طوعا، وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم كرها

THALABI:v9p152#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p152#2/r5.speaker: أبو رمتة
THALABI:v9p152#2/r5.claim: Abū Rimtha reports that the Prophet told him that neither father nor son bears the other's sin, then recited that no bearer carries another's burden.
THALABI:v9p152#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي رمتة، قال: انطلقت مع أبي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما رأيته قال لي أبي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r3.claim: No soul is held accountable for another soul's sin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r3.anchor: أي: لا تؤخذ نفس بمأثم غيرها

QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.claim: No one bears another's burden because reward and punishment arise from settled dispositions formed by repeated good or bad acts; immediate allotted fortunes also depend on divine decree, but the proximate cause counts.
QASHANI:53:37-39/r3.anchor: لأن العقاب يترتب على هيئات مظلمة رسخت في النفس بتكرار الأفاعيل والأقاويل السيئة

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r7.claim: The central intent is to state the afterlife rule that no soul bears another's burden.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r7.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh asıl murad hükm-i uhrevîyi beyandır.

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r8.claim: The particle an is lightened, with the pronoun of شأن omitted, so the construction means wa-annahu.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r8.anchor: ki doğrusu bu اَن muhaffefedir, zamîr-i şan mahzuf olup

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r1.claim: Vizr means sin and a heavy burden; here it means sin and bearing its punishment, so no one pays another's afterlife penalty.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r1.anchor: günah ve ağır yük mânasına gelir ki burada günah ve günahın cezâsını çekmek mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r2.claim: The legal maxim is that punishment cannot be delegated: each person bears their own offense, and cannot rescue another by taking that person's sin.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r2.anchor: Bunun ta‘bîr-i fıkhîsi “ukūbâtta niyâbet câri olmaz” kā‘ide-i külliyesidir.

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r3.claim: A person who undertakes another's burden instead incurs their own added burden, as stated in 29:13.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r3.anchor: belki kendi taahhüdünün cezâsını çeker وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًۭا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r4.claim: The hadith says whoever establishes a bad practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act on it until Judgment Day.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r4.anchor: مَنْ سَ َّن سُن َّةً سَي ِّئَةً فـَعَلَيْهِ وِزْرُهَا وَوِزْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا إلَى يـَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r2.claim: Responsibility is individual: no one can bear another person’s sin, even if they wished to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r2.anchor: suçların ve cezaların şahsîliği esastır; –istese de– kimse başkasının günahını yüklenemez

AKHFASH:v2p526/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p526/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p526/r6.claim: An lā taziru is an appositional substitute for the phrase about what is in Moses' scriptures, meaning that no bearer bears another's burden.
AKHFASH:v2p526/r6.anchor: فقوله {أن لا تزر} بدل من قوله {بما في صحف موسى} [36]

NAHHAS:v4p276/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r7.claim: The clause can be accusative as an appositive to mā, or nominative as a new clause meaning that no bearer bears another's burden; wazara means to carry a burden.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r7.anchor: أن في موضع نصب على البدل من ما ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r4.claim: The clause may be genitive as a replacement for ما: he was informed that no bearer bears another's burden.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r4.anchor: المعنى أم لم ينبأ بأن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r5.claim: Alternatively أن is nominative with an implicit هو, as the answer to what is in the scrolls.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " أن " في موضع رفع على إضمار " هو " كأنه

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r6.claim: No person is held for another person's sin.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r6.anchor: ومعناه ولا تؤخذ نفس بإثم غيرها

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r7.claim: The verb تزر is from وزر يزز, to incur a burden of sin.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r7.anchor: وتزر من وزر يزز إذا كسب وزرا وهو الإثم

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r6.claim: An is either the lightened emphatic particle, genitive as apposition to ‘in the pages,’ or nominative as the predicate of an implied ‘it is.’

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.claim: No one is held accountable for another person's sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r7.anchor: والمعنى أنه لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.claim: This does not conflict with the killing verse or the report that an originator of an evil practice bears its burden and others' burdens: causing others to follow is the originator's own culpable act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r8.anchor: فإن ذلك للدلالة والتسبب الذي هو وزره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r9.claim: No soul bears another’s sin; one cannot offload either the guilt of turning away or that of what follows it onto someone else.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r9.anchor: ألا تزر } أي تأثم وتحمل { وازرة } أي نفس بلغت مبلغا تكون فيه حاملة { وزر أخرى * } أي حملها الثقيل من الإثم

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say Abraham fulfilled the command to convey the statement that no bearer bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} قال: بلغ هذه الآية {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham completed obedience in what he did with his son after the dream, and fulfilled the statement in Moses's scrolls that no bearer bears another's burden.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} يقول: الذي استكمل الطاعة فيما فعل بابنه حين رأى الرؤيا والذي في صحف موسى {ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r3.claim: No bearer carries another’s burden; each is taken for their own sins, so al-Walīd was wrong to pay another to bear his liability.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r3.anchor: أنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، أي لا تحمل حاملة حمل أخرى، وإنما يؤخذ كل واحد بذنوب نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.claim: Before Abraham, an ally could be held for a killing; Abraham fulfilled and conveyed the rule that no bearer carries another’s burden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كانوا قبل إبراهيم يأخذون الولي بالولي في القتل ونحوه فوفى إبراهيم وبلغ هذا الحكم من أنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r14.claim: Wizr means a burden or weight.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r15.claim: The feminine wazira either means a soul or is intensive, like ʿallāma and nasāba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r15.anchor: وأنث الوازرة إما لأنه أراد النفس وإما أراد المبالغة كعلامة ونسابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r16.claim: أن is the light form of the emphatic particle, effectively meaning أنه لا تزر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r16.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة، وتقديرها أنه لا تزر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r17.claim: An intervening element is acceptable while the verb remains indicative, as in the cited construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r17.anchor: وحسن الحائل بينها وبين الفعل إن بقي الفعل مرتفعا، فهي كقوله: أن سيكون منكم مرضى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r18.claim: أن may occupy a nominative or genitive syntactic position; both parses are valid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r18.anchor: و «أن» في موضع رفع أو خفض، كلاهما مرتب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r1.claim: These pages teach that each soul bears its own wrongs, whether disbelief or other sins, and no one carries another's burden, as in 35:18.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p465/r1.anchor: أي: كل نفس ظلمت نفسها بكفر أو شيء من الذنوب فإنما عليها وزرها، لا يحمله عنها أحد

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r7.claim: Wizr means a burden; sin is called a burden because it weighs on its bearer.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r7.anchor: والوزر: الثقل، وسمي الذنب وزرا؛ لأنه يثقل على صاحبه

JISHUMI:v9p6660/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r13.claim: Wāz ira is feminine because the wording refers back to the feminine noun nafs.
JISHUMI:v9p6660/r13.anchor: إنما قال: وازرة؛ لأنه ردها إلى النفس

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid say Abraham fulfilled his task by conveying that no bearer bears another's burden; Ibn ʿAbbās says he prohibited an earlier custom of transferring sins among kin and neighbors.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r4.anchor: وقيل: وفى في تبليغ الرسالة التي هي قوله: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r13.claim: No one carries another person's punishment or sin; the wording says no bearer carries another's burden.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r13.anchor: أي: لا يحمل على أحد عقاب غيره ولا ذنبه. ونظم الآية: ولا يحمل حامل حمل غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r4.claim: أن is a lightened heavy particle, meaning no bearer bears another's burden; its clause is genitive as a substitute for ما or nominative as the predicate of an implied هو.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r4.anchor: أن مخففة من الثقيلة . والمعنى : أنه لا تزر

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r6.claim: No soul bears the sin of another soul.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r6.anchor: { ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } [آية: 38] يقول: لا تحمل نفس خطيئة نفس أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.claim: An is the lightened emphatic particle; it is genitive as an apposition to mā, or nominative with implicit huwa.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r3.anchor: المخففة من الثقيلة وموضعها جر بدلا من «ما»

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham conveyed that no bearer carries another's burden; before him people were punished for relatives' sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا قبل إبراهيم عليه السلام يأخذون الرجل بذنب غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r12.speaker: أبو مالك الغفاري
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r12.claim: Abu Malik says the passage from no bearer carrying another's burden through which of the Lord's favors people dispute is in Abraham's and Moses' scrolls.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r12.anchor: وقال أبو مالك الغفاري قوله تعالى: { ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى }

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi points to his fuller discussion of this principle in al-Anʿam.
